neighbours.label: radial geometry: lines or features spreading outward from a common centre ('radiate out', 'like spokes', 'radially', 'bulls-eye'); heat radiating and parallel or straight layouts stay quiet
fire: From the central plaza, broad avenues radiate outward in every direction.
The cracks in the windshield spread out like spokes from the point of impact.
The petals are arranged radially around a small yellow disk.
Seen from above, the old town's streets radiate from the cathedral like a star.
The target's rings formed a bulls-eye, with each band circling the center.
Railway lines radiate out from the capital to every province.
On the map, the canals fan out from the harbor like the spokes of a wheel.
The spider built its web with threads radiating from a single point.
quiet: From the central plaza, a single avenue runs north to the river.
The cracks in the windshield ran in one long line from side to side.
The petals are arranged in two neat rows along the stem.
Seen from above, the old town's streets form a regular square grid.
The target was a plain square of cardboard taped to the fence.
Railway lines run parallel to the coast for most of the province.
On the map, the canals run side by side through the harbor district.
The radiator gave off a steady warmth that filled the small room.
